column3: Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew oath says “thus may the gods do, and thus may they add,” without an explicit “with me.” It compares his life with that of “one of them”; BSB supplies “with me” and uses plural lives with an explicit reference to those killed.
The Hebrew says that he saw, rose, and went for his life; BSB names Elijah and says that he was afraid and ran.
The Hebrew explicitly says “one broom tree” and “now” in the request to die; BSB leaves these words implicit.
The Hebrew says “one broom tree”; BSB says “the broom tree.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives the journey’s greatness as the reason, using “for”; BSB frames it as an alternative consequence, using “or.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed and calls it “the cave”; BSB names Elijah and says “a cave.”
The Hebrew says “sons of Israel” and explicitly states the purpose of taking his life; BSB uses “Israelites” and “seeking my life as well.”
The Hebrew leaves the initial speaker unnamed; BSB supplies “the LORD.”
The Hebrew uses the expression “a sound of thin silence”; BSB renders it as “a still, small voice.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “sons of Israel” and explicitly states the purpose of taking his life; BSB uses “Israelites” and “seeking my life as well.”
The Hebrew says to return on his way toward the wilderness of Damascus; BSB expands this as the way he came and a further command to go to the Desert of Damascus.
The Hebrew repeats the anointing verb for Elisha; BSB leaves that second occurrence implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “all the knees” and singular “all the mouth”; BSB supplies their possessors and uses plural “mouths.”
The Hebrew leaves the departing subject unnamed and says that the twelve teams were before him; BSB names Elijah and leaves that position implicit.
The Hebrew leaves both speakers unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha and Elijah. BSB also adds “goodbye” to the requested kiss.
The Hebrew leaves the returning man unnamed and separately says he rose, followed Elijah, and served him; BSB names Elisha and makes following and serving the purpose of setting out.
